description: Native Markdown resilience plan for the fictional city of Harbor Point, exercising heading/block anchors, repeated subsection names, and a Markdown table.

source.source_label: Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan
source.provenance: Synthetic document written for this golden set. Every place, organisation, and figure is fictional.

facts.statement: The Harbor Point City Council adopted the plan on 14 March 2026.

evidence.text: The plan was adopted by the Harbor Point City Council on 14 March 2026.

facts.statement: Harbor Point recorded 23 days above 35 °C in 2025, against a 1991-2020 average of 9 days per year.

evidence.text: Harbor Point recorded 23 days above 35 °C in 2025, compared with an average of 9 such days per year between 1991 and 2020.

facts.statement: Street flooding affects 37 intersections during a 10-year rainfall event.

evidence.text: Street flooding affects 37 intersections during a 10-year rainfall event.

facts.statement: The plan will plant 4,800 street trees along 12 cool corridors in Eastside and Millbrook.

evidence.text: The plan will plant 4,800 street trees along 12 cool corridors connecting schools, clinics, and transit stops in Eastside and Millbrook.

facts.statement: The plan will build 85 bioretention cells and convert 3.2 hectares of asphalt schoolyards.

evidence.text: The plan will build 85 bioretention cells and convert 3.2 hectares of asphalt schoolyards into permeable green play areas.

facts.statement: The programme costs USD 26.5 million, of which USD 18.6 million is sought from external grants.

evidence.text: The total programme cost is USD 26.5 million. Harbor Point will contribute USD 7.9 million from its capital budget, and the plan seeks USD 18.6 million in external grant funding.

facts.statement: Cool corridors are estimated at USD 9.6 million.

evidence.text: Cool corridor planting and three years of establishment watering are estimated at USD 9.6 million.

facts.statement: The city will designate 18 community cooling centres.

evidence.text: The Office of Climate Resilience will designate 18 community cooling centres in libraries and recreation centres, with extended opening hours on days above 32 °C.
